doc.name: StartupHub.ai
doc.instructions: Look up startups, investors, and people. Use query_funding for how much a country or sector raised in a year. Use discover_email or validate_email for a work address, and only report an address the tool returned. Content jobs that return a job id are unfinished until the matching get call reports status done. Submit and update tools change records the signed-in account is allowed to change. Do not invent funding, headcount, scores, or emails.

tools.name: search_startups
tools.description: Search the startup database with any combination of filters: name, sector, country, city radius, founded date, team size, the latest funding round (round_series, raised_after), total funding, valuation, investors (backed_by), StartupHub score, Agent Readiness score, tech stack, website state, stealth status and known founder emails. Each result includes the latest round (last_round_series, last_round_date), sectors, HQ, founded date and score; paid plans add funding totals, headcount and more. Example: round_series=Seed, raised_after=2026-10-01, sort=last_round_date.desc for companies that just raised a seed round. Returns up to 100 per call (1 db credit); page with offset. Pairs with list_startup_team and discover_email to turn each result into a contactable lead. Needs a StartupHub.ai account: a free account includes 50 lookups a month.

q.description: Search text, matched against the name and one-liner.

slugs.description: Comma-separated StartupHub slugs, up to 100, lowercased before matching; matches any of them. Fetches known companies in one call.

sector.description: Comma-separated sector names, e.g. "Fintech,Cybersecurity"; matches any of them. Exact sector names as shown on profiles.

country.description: Comma-separated countries; matches any of them. Accepts names or ISO codes; "US", "USA" and "United States" are the same.

status.description: Operating status. Exact, case-sensitive match on the stored value, for example Active or Inactive.

founded_after.description: Founded on or after this date: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD.

founded_before.description: Founded on or before this date: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD.

near.description: HQ inside a bounding box around a point: "lat,lng,radius_km", radius clamped to 1-500 km. A malformed value applies no filter. Example "51.507,-0.128,25" for central London.

employees_max.description: Maximum employee count (inclusive). Use 10 for tiny teams.

min_linkedin_followers.description: Minimum LinkedIn followers, a brand-size proxy when headcount is unknown.

hiring.description: 'true' returns only companies with open roles right now.

round_series.description: Comma-separated stages of the most recent funding round; matches any of them. Values: Angel, Pre-Seed, Seed, Pre-Series A, Series A to Series H, Growth, Debt, Grant, Strategic, IPO. Pair with raised_after for "just raised a seed round".

raised_after.description: Most recent funding round announced on or after this date: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD.

raised_before.description: Most recent funding round announced on or before this date: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD.

min_valuation.description: Minimum latest valuation, USD. 1000000000 for unicorns.

backed_by.description: Comma-separated investors, up to 20, by StartupHub slug or exact name, e.g. "sequoia-capital,Y Combinator"; matches any of them. When none of them matches an investor, the response is empty data plus a note.

ma_status.description: Comma-separated exit states: acquired, public, merged, made_acquisitions; matches any of them.

min_score.description: Minimum StartupHub score (0-100). 70+ is roughly the top 1.5%.

min_agent_readiness.description: Minimum Agent Readiness score (0-100): how well AI agents can use the company website.

agent_readiness_grade.description: Comma-separated Agent Readiness grades: A+, A, B, C, D, F; matches any of them.

trending.description: 'true' returns companies getting attention on StartupHub this week.

mentioned_since.description: Covered in StartupHub news on or after this date: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD.

min_reddit_reviews.description: Minimum number of classified Reddit reviews.

min_reddit_sentiment.description: Minimum Reddit sentiment, -100 to 100. Pair with min_reddit_reviews.

has_founders.description: 'true' returns only companies with known founders, ready for list_startup_team.

has_known_emails.description: 'true' returns only companies with at least one verified founder or team email. Startup and up; Startup sees redacted addresses, Pro sees them in full.

has_website.description: 'true' returns only companies with a website on file.

has_blog.description: 'true' returns only companies whose website has a blog or news feed we found (RSS or Atom), 'false' only those checked and without one. Sites are rechecked every 90 days.

blog_post_within_days.description: Only companies whose blog published a post within this many days (30, 90 or 365 are the usual values). Implies has_blog=true.

website_status.description: Comma-separated website states: active, dead, parked; matches any of them.

domain_tld.description: Comma-separated domain endings, e.g. "ai,io"; matches any of them.

stealth.description: 'true' = stealth only, 'false' = exclude stealth. Stealth rows need Startup or higher.

cdn.description: Comma-separated CDNs: cloudflare, vercel, cloudfront, fastly, netlify; matches any of them.

email_provider.description: Comma-separated email providers: google_workspace, m365, zoho, proton, proofpoint, mimecast, self_hosted, gateway; matches any of them.

hosting.description: Comma-separated hosting providers: aws, azure, gcp, vercel, render, netlify, hetzner, digitalocean; matches any of them.

payment.description: Comma-separated payment providers: stripe, paddle, lemonsqueezy, paypal, klarna, apple_pay; matches any of them. The API also accepts payments as an alias.

compliance.description: Comma-separated compliance claims found on the site: soc2, hipaa, iso27001, gdpr, ccpa, pci_dss, fedramp; matches any of them.

status_page.description: Comma-separated status page vendors: statuspage, instatus, betterstack; matches any of them.

cookie_consent.description: Comma-separated cookie consent vendors: onetrust, cookiebot, osano, termly; matches any of them.

hiring_platform.description: Comma-separated hiring platforms: greenhouse, lever, ashby, workable, teamtailor; matches any of them.

booking.description: Comma-separated booking widgets: calendly, calcom, savvycal, chilipiper; matches any of them.

email_marketing.description: Comma-separated email marketing tools: klaviyo, mailchimp, hubspot_forms, customer_io, loops; matches any of them.

ai_support.description: Comma-separated AI customer support tools: intercom_fin, ada, sierra, decagon, drift_ai, fin_ai; matches any of them.

a11y.description: Comma-separated accessibility overlays: userway, accessibe, audioeye; matches any of them.

affiliate_program.description: Comma-separated affiliate platforms: partnerstack, rewardful, tolt, firstpromoter, impact; matches any of them.

has_affiliate_program.description: 'true' returns only companies running an affiliate program.

sort.description: '<column>.<asc|desc>'. Columns: total_score, created_at (when StartupHub added the row), last_round_date, latest_funding_date (alias of last_round_date), total_funding, latest_valuation, founded_date, employee_count, employee_growth_quarterly_cagr, linkedin_followers, agent_readiness_score, trending_score_7d, current_revenue, revenue_multiple, revenue_per_employee, funding_efficiency. Default total_score.desc. An unknown column falls back to total_score.desc, and any direction other than asc sorts descending.

offset.description: Skip this many results, to page past the first 100.

tools.title: Search startups

tools.name: find_stealth_startups
tools.description: Convenience wrapper around search_startups pre-tuned for fresh-stealth deal-flow. Always sends stealth=true and sort=founded_date.desc; those two cannot be changed here. Returns stealth startups with their detected tech stack (CDN, email provider, analytics), RDAP domain registration date, and a has_known_emails flag indicating whether at least one founder/team email has been verified. Inputs: domain_tld (default 'ai,io,so,xyz,security'), with_emails (default true, which sends has_known_emails=true; pass false to drop that filter), founded_after, country, cdn, email_provider, limit (default 20, max 100). There is no offset; use search_startups with stealth=true to page further. Startup tier and higher only (Free tier 403s). Startup sees redacted emails; Pro tier sees full. Combine with list_startup_team and discover_email to surface the actual addresses. Needs a StartupHub.ai account: a free account includes 50 lookups a month.

domain_tld.description: Comma-separated TLDs. Defaults to 'ai,io,so,xyz,security' (the high-signal AI-native TLDs).

with_emails.description: When true (default), only return startups with at least one verified founder/team email (has_known_emails=true). False drops that filter.

founded_after.description: Only stealth startups founded on or after this date: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD.

country.description: Optional comma-separated HQ countries, names or ISO codes.

email_provider.description: Optional comma-separated email_provider filter (e.g. 'm365,self_hosted' to find non-Google-Workspace stealth shops).

tools.title: Find stealth startups

tools.name: search_domains
tools.description: Domain radar: newly registered names from our discovery queue (NRD, registries, GitHub orgs). This is NOT a company profile. Returns apex, registration date, registrar, mailbox signal, quality score, and status (queued / quality_failed). startup_slug is set only after we promote a real homepage into the directory. Always sorted newest first (created_at desc). Use search_startups for companies. Any plan: on a free key the first 10 domains a day are free, then 1 credit per 5 domains; paid plans use their included credits. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

tld.description: Comma-separated TLDs, e.g. 'ai,io'. Only ai, io, xyz, so, com and security filter anything; other values apply no filter. Maps to the NRD/CT sources and combines with source by OR.

source.description: Comma-separated raw source or bucket ids, e.g. 'dot_ai_nrd', 'dot_ai_zone', 'github_new_org', 'uk_companies_house'.

status.description: Comma-separated: queued, quality_failed, promoted, rejected. Default is queued,quality_failed.

apex.description: Exact hostname lookup, e.g. acme.ai. A leading www. is stripped; a value with no dot returns 400 invalid_apex. Overrides q.

q.description: Substring match on apex or candidate name. Needs at least 2 characters after removing % _ and commas, otherwise no filter.

created_after.description: ISO date. Rows we first ingested on or after this time.

created_before.description: ISO date. Rows we first ingested on or before this time.

has_real_email.description: Mailbox on the domain (MX is not empty).

has_real_content.description: Last homepage probe found real body copy.

promoted.description: 'true' = only names that already have a public startup profile.

offset.description: Skip this many rows, for paging.

tools.title: Search new domains

tools.name: get_startup
tools.description: Get full profile for a startup by slug Needs a StartupHub.ai account: a free account includes 50 lookups a month.
tools.title: Get startup profile

tools.name: get_startup_by_domain
tools.description: Look up a single startup by its website domain. Accepts raw URLs (https://www.example.com/about), stripped (example.com), with or without paths. Returns the full profile. Use match_companies_by_domain instead for batches of 2+ domains. Needs a StartupHub.ai account: a free account includes 50 lookups a month.
tools.title: Get startup by domain

tools.name: scan_company_technology
tools.description: Tech Stack Checker. Return hosting, frameworks, analytics, payments, and mail setup for a company website. Checks a stored fingerprint first, then a fresh live read when live=true. Accepts a URL or a plain domain. Costs 1 credit. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

domain.description: Company domain or URL, e.g. "anthropic.com" or "https://anthropic.com/about"

live.description: When true, force a fresh live scan even if a cached DB fingerprint exists.

tools.title: Scan company tech stack

tools.name: get_startup_socials
tools.description: Lightweight endpoint that returns ONLY a startup's contact emails (contact / partnerships / press) and social URLs (LinkedIn, Twitter, GitHub, Facebook, YouTube, Discord, Slack, etc.) plus HQ city/country. Cheaper than get_startup (1 db credit vs 1 profile credit) when you don't need the full row. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).
tools.title: Get startup socials & emails

tools.name: get_person_by_email
tools.description: Reverse-lookup a person profile by their email address. Pairs naturally with discover_email + validate_email: discover an email, verify it, find the person record. Returns the full person profile. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).
tools.title: Look up person by email

tools.name: get_person_by_social
tools.description: Reverse-lookup a person profile by any of their social URLs/handles. Pass linkedin, twitter, or github (full URL like https://www.linkedin.com/in/foo, OR just the handle 'foo'). Multiple params allowed: first match wins. Returns the full person profile + which platform matched. Needs a StartupHub.ai account: a free account includes 50 lookups a month.

linkedin.description: LinkedIn URL or handle (e.g. https://www.linkedin.com/in/foo or just "foo")

twitter.description: Twitter/X URL or handle (e.g. https://x.com/foo or "@foo")

tools.title: Look up person by social

tools.name: get_investor_by_domain
tools.description: Look up a single investor (VC, angel, accelerator) by their website domain. Same shape as get_startup_by_domain, against the investors table. Useful when you have a fund's website and want fund profile / portfolio info. Needs a StartupHub.ai account: a free account includes 50 lookups a month.
tools.title: Get investor by domain

tools.name: get_investor_by_social
tools.description: Reverse-lookup an investor profile by their LinkedIn or Twitter URL/handle. Investor LinkedIns are typically /company/<slug>, but the lookup handles both /in/ and /company/ patterns. Needs a StartupHub.ai account: a free account includes 50 lookups a month.
tools.title: Look up investor by social

tools.name: get_startup_funding_history
tools.description: Full chronological list of investment rounds for a startup: amount, series, date, pre/post-money valuation, lead and participating investor IDs, plus a summary with total raised from rounds and the latest round date/series. Use after get_startup if you need round-by-round detail rather than just total_funding. Needs a StartupHub.ai account: a free account includes 50 lookups a month.
tools.title: Get startup funding history

tools.name: list_startup_team
tools.description: Returns founders, current team, and board members for a startup, split by role. Each person record includes name, title, slug, LinkedIn, Twitter, description, and primary_email if visible to your plan tier. Use this to build org-charts, identify decision-makers for outreach, or enrich a startup record with its known people. Needs a StartupHub.ai account: a free account includes 50 lookups a month.
tools.title: List startup team

tools.name: enrich_email
tools.description: One-call CRM/inbox enrichment. Pass an email, get back: the best available name and its source, the person's public Gravatar profile when they have one (name, title, company, location, verified social accounts), the domain's mail provider, matched person record (if known), the email's domain matched against startups + investors (with funding intel for VC-backed scoring), a heuristic name guess from the local part if person is unknown, and a flag for free email providers (gmail/outlook/etc) so you can skip company matching on consumer addresses. The killer endpoint for HubSpot/Salesforce auto-enrichment, Gmail/Outlook plugins, and lead-scoring pipelines. 1 profile credit (cheaper than chaining get_person_by_email + get_startup_by_domain + get_investor_by_domain separately). Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).
tools.title: Enrich an email address

tools.name: search_investors
tools.description: Find investors that match a startup's profile. Filter by sector_focus (e.g. 'Artificial Intelligence' for AI investors), stage_focus (Seed / Series A / etc.), geo_focus, cheque_min / cheque_max (matches investors whose cheque-size window overlaps the founder's raise), active_since (investors whose latest investment is on or after this date, to surface who has deployed capital recently), min_recent_rounds_90d (activity threshold), and actively_investing. Sort whitelist: total_score, last_investment_date, recent_rounds_90d, recent_lead_rounds_90d, total_funds_raised, min_cheque_size, max_cheque_size, last_mentioned_at, created_at. For example sort='last_investment_date.desc' surfaces the most recently active funds first. Page with offset. Needs a StartupHub.ai account: a free account includes 50 lookups a month.

type.description: Exact, case-sensitive match on the stored investor type, for example VC, Angel, Accelerator, Corporate VC, Family Office, PE.

sector_focus.description: Sector the investor focuses on (e.g. 'Artificial Intelligence', 'Biotech', 'Fintech'). Comma-separated values must all be present.

stage_focus.description: Funding stage (e.g. 'Seed', 'Series A'). Comma-separated values must all be present.

geo_focus.description: Geographic region the investor targets (e.g. "US", "Europe", "Israel"). Comma-separated values must all be present.

cheque_min.description: Founder's minimum target raise: matches investors whose max_cheque_size is at least this amount

cheque_max.description: Founder's maximum target raise: matches investors whose min_cheque_size is at most this amount

active_since.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Returns investors whose latest investment is on or after this date.

min_recent_rounds_90d.description: Minimum number of rounds in the last 90 days. Use 1+ to drop dormant funds.

actively_investing.description: Only true filters; false applies no filter.

sort.description: Sort order: '<column>.<asc|desc>' from the whitelist above. Default total_score.desc. An unknown column falls back to the default.

offset.description: Skip this many results, for paging.

tools.title: Search investors

tools.name: search_people
tools.description: Search founders, executives, board members, and key team members. Results are sorted by StartupHub score, highest first. Page with offset. Needs a StartupHub.ai account: a free account includes 50 lookups a month.

title.description: Partial match on the current title, e.g. CTO.

sector.description: One exact sector name; commas are not split into several sectors.

tag.description: One tag, e.g. Unit 8200, Unit 81, Serial Entrepreneur, AI Expert, Investor, Has Exits.

offset.description: Skip this many results, for paging.

tools.title: Search people

tools.name: call_api
tools.description: Call any API, MCP server, chat endpoint or agent listed on StartupHub (find one with find_apis), billed to your StartupHub credits. REST: operation "METHOD /path" plus path, query, body. MCP: operation = tool name plus arguments. Chat: operation = model id plus messages. Agent: task; a long agent task answers with a task_id, follow it with get_api_task. label names what the call is for in your console. Add provider_key only when the listing needs your own key for that service. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

provider_key.description: Your key for that service, used for this call only

label.description: What this call is for, e.g. "book the reservation". Shown in your console.

tools.title: call api

tools.name: list_my_api
tools.description: List an API, MCP server, model endpoint or A2A agent on one of your own StartupHub profiles, so people and agents can find, try and pay for it. Check first with preview: true (nothing saved). kind: openapi (spec URL), mcp (server URL), chat (OpenAI-compatible base URL), agent (site or agent card URL), app (site, link only). Optional price_per_call in USD (free if omitted), provider_key to sell calls through StartupHub (stored encrypted; you earn the price less 20%). Returns the listing id. Never creates an account: the key must belong to the profile owner. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

startup_id.description: Your profile id (my_apis returns the profiles you can list on)

startup_slug.description: Or your profile slug, e.g. acme-ai from startuphub.ai/startups/acme-ai

preview.description: Only read what the URL offers, save nothing

tools.title: list my api

tools.name: my_apis
tools.description: Your API directory listings with calls and earnings this month, and the profiles you can list on. Pass recheck_id to re-read a listing from its URL after you changed the spec, tools or agent card, or remove_id to take one down. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).
tools.title: my apis

tools.name: get_api_task
tools.description: Check a long-running task: a task_id from call_api or a route_id from run_agent_task. Returns its state, which agents were tried, and the output once it is done. Pass cancel to stop it (credits come back) or reply to answer an agent that asked for input. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

reply.description: Your answer when the task needs input

tools.title: get api task

tools.name: run_agent_task
tools.description: Give a task and StartupHub picks the agent to run it: listed agents and models are ranked on fit to the task, success rate and speed from real calls, and price. If the chosen agent fails, the task moves to the next one, and failed attempts are refunded, so you pay only for the agent that finished it. Billed to your StartupHub credits. Long tasks return a route_id: follow it with get_api_task. dry_run shows the ranking without running anything. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

task.description: What you want done, in plain words

label.description: What this is for, e.g. "book the reservation". Shown in your console.

max_price_usd.description: Skip agents priced above this per task

listing_ids.description: Only choose among these listings (ids from find_apis)

fallbacks.description: How many other agents to try if one fails, 0-3, default 2

tools.title: run agent task

tools.name: spend_limits
tools.description: Cap what you spend through StartupHub per day or per month: on everything, on one listing, or on one label. Calls stop at the limit, and you get an alert when spend passes alert_pct (80% by default). With no arguments, lists your limits and what is spent so far. Set: period plus limit_credits, optionally listing_id or label. Remove: remove_id. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).
tools.title: spend limits

tools.name: find_logo
tools.description: Find square and horizontal logos for a company Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).
tools.title: Find company logo

tools.name: find_apis
tools.description: Find APIs, MCP servers and AI agents listed on StartupHub by the companies that run them. Returns each one's endpoint, spec URL, auth type, price per call and operations, tools, models or skills, plus call_through_startuphub: a URL that runs the call with your StartupHub key and credits. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

query.description: What the API should do, or a company name

kind.description: openapi = REST APIs, mcp = MCP servers, chat = OpenAI-compatible endpoints, agent = A2A agents, app = apps without an API, agents = chat + agent + app

tools.title: find apis

tools.name: enrich_company
tools.description: Build a company profile from a name and optional website or LinkedIn URL. Returns the description, sector, headquarters, founding year, and public links that were found. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).
tools.title: AI-enrich a company

tools.name: validate_email
tools.description: Verify if a single email address is real and deliverable. Returns {valid, status, confidence_score}. Use when you already know the address (e.g. from a contact page, LinkedIn, or a prior discover_email run) and want to confirm it before sending. To go from a person's name → verified email instead, use discover_email: that already runs validation internally on every candidate, so don't call validate_email on its output. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).
tools.title: Validate an email

tools.name: discover_email
tools.description: Find a real, deliverable professional email for a person at a company. Pass first name + last name + the company domain; get back the verified address, a confidence score, and a short note about who it likely reaches. Charges 1 credit only when an address is found. May take a moment on first call — if the response comes back with no matches, call this tool again with the same args and the answer typically returns instantly. Pairs naturally with scan_agent_readiness for outbound prospecting: scan a prospect's site for a 0-100 AI-readiness score, find the owner via web search, then call this tool for the verified email — the readiness gaps become the outreach hook. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

role.description: Optional: the person's role, e.g. CEO or co-founder. A confirmed first-name address for a founder or CEO is rated high confidence.

tools.title: Discover a professional email

tools.name: match_companies_by_domain
tools.description: Bulk-match an array of advertiser/company domains against StartupHub.ai's startup database. Returns per-domain whether the company is in our database, plus funding amount, latest round, investor IDs, sectors, founded date, and HQ country. Built for cross-reference workflows like 'what % of Google Ads / Taboola / Outbrain advertisers are VC-backed': pass a scraped advertiser list, get back the funding intel. Up to 100 domains per call, 1 db credit per request (only charged when matches found). Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

domains.description: Array of advertiser/company domains. Accepts raw URLs (https://www.example.com), stripped (example.com), with or without paths. Max 100 per call.

tools.title: Match companies by domain

tools.name: list_credit_packs
tools.description: Get credit pack pricing AND a checkout URL the user can open to buy more credits. Returns { buy_url: 'https://www.startuphub.ai/pricing?buy=credits', pricing: { validate: [...tiers], discover: [...tiers] } }: surface the buy_url to the user when they hit a 402 'credit_limit_exceeded' error or ask 'how do I get more credits'. There is no in-MCP purchase flow (Stripe checkout requires a browser); your job is to show the price tiers and hand them the buy_url. Credits never expire and volume discounts auto-apply.
tools.title: List credit pack pricing

tools.name: get_my_usage
tools.description: Check the user's current credit balance: plan tier, daily + monthly limits per credit type (validate, discover, db, profile, logo, enrich, submit), used today, remaining today, used this month, remaining this month, and any never-expiring credit pack balance. Free to call (does NOT charge a credit): call before any expensive batch (e.g. 100x discover_email) so the user knows whether they need to top up first. If they're low or ask to buy more, follow up with list_credit_packs to get pricing + a checkout URL. Requires Bearer auth; anonymous callers get a 401 with a signup link. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).
tools.title: Check credit balance & usage

tools.name: scan_agent_readiness
tools.description: Scans a public site against current AI-agent readiness standards, including the llms.txt v2 shape (H1, summary, described links, and whether those links resolve). Returns a 0-100 score plus per-check pass/fail with a copy-paste fix prompt for each gap. A link to startuphub.ai in llms.txt or on the homepage is an 8-point bonus and is not required. Free, no credits charged. Common workflow: when a user wants leads who *need* AI-readiness work, search the web for businesses in a category/region, scan each site, then use discover_email on the lowest-scoring ones: the failed checks are the cold-outreach hook ('your site scores 23/100, here's what's missing'). Also useful as a self-audit for the user's own sites. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

url.description: The site to scan, e.g. https://example.com

tools.title: Scan AI-agent readiness

tools.name: rate_this_service
tools.description: Optional. Rate how well StartupHub.ai served this task, 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent), with a short reason. Ratings are counted by agent type in a public monthly report and are never shown as customer reviews. Free, no API key.

reason.description: One sentence: what worked or what was missing.

would_pay.description: Would this task be worth paying for per call.

tools.title: Rate this service

tools.name: get_trends
tools.description: Get a structured, real-time snapshot of what's happening in the AI startup ecosystem right now — capital deployed this week, top sectors and countries (with week-over-week change), biggest rounds, stage breakdown with median check sizes, emerging themes (3+ companies clustering on the same narrow problem), most active investors, and exits. Sourced from StartupHub.ai's database (25k+ startups, 24k+ funding rounds). Use this when a user asks what's trending in AI/startups, to build an investment thesis, to spot rotations, or for weekly-digest-style summaries. Free tool — no API key needed. Returns structured JSON the caller can format into tables, charts, or narrative. Needs a StartupHub.ai account: a free account includes 50 lookups a month.
tools.title: Get AI startup trends

tools.name: query_funding
tools.description: Answer how much funding was raised, how many rounds closed, or how many companies were founded, for a country, sector, series, and year. This is the StartupHub /analysis chart as data. Use it for questions like 'how much funding did Canadian startups raise in 2026'. dataset=rounds (default) is announced round capital in that year. dataset=startups is companies founded that year, and the dollar total is what those companies have raised to date, not capital raised during the year. dataset=funds is fund closes. dataset=investors counts firms founded, with no dollar total. country is a full English name: Canada, United States, United Kingdom. group=sector or group=country returns a breakdown. Free, no API key. Returns the count, total USD, a chart URL, and the periods or categories behind the total. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

country.description: Full English country name, or a common alias. Examples: Canada, United States, USA, United Kingdom, UK. Comma-separated for more than one, up to 8.

sector.description: Sector name, for example Artificial Intelligence or Fintech. Comma-separated for more than one, up to 8.

series.description: Round stage, dataset=rounds only. Exact, case-sensitive values: Pre-Seed, Seed, Series A, Series B, Series C, Series D, Series E, Series F+, Growth, IPO, Debt, Grant, Strategic, Unlabeled. Comma-separated for more than one. Any other value is dropped.

year.description: Calendar year, an integer from 1970 to 2100. Sets both from and to. Example: 2026.

from.description: First year, inclusive. Ignored when year is set. Default depends on dataset: rounds 2021, funds 2015, startups 2010, investors 1995. Clamped to the dataset range.

to.description: Last year, inclusive. Ignored when year is set. Default the current year. Clamped between from and the current year.

dataset.description: rounds = capital announced in the year (default). startups = companies founded that year. funds = funds closed. investors = firms founded.

group.description: How to break the total down. Default time, which is the single undivided total. Depends on dataset: funds and startups have no series; investors allows only time, sector and country. An invalid value becomes time. group=sector counts a company in every sector it carries, so that total is higher.

bucket.description: Time bucket. A single year defaults to year. A range defaults to quarter.

split.description: Optional second breakdown: one of the dataset dimensions, not equal to group. Anything else means none. The total still excludes double-counting.

tools.name: get_arbitrage
tools.description: Live cross-venue prediction-market arbitrage board. Returns the same real-world events priced on Polymarket, Kalshi/Robinhood, and PredictIt side by side, with a real arbitrage flagged whenever the combined cost of locking a $1 payout drops under $1 (is_arbitrage=true, with roi_pct + profit_per_dollar). Each opportunity carries both legs (venue, price, direct trade URL), the combined cost, and when the arb last opened. Refreshed every 30 minutes. Pass arbs_only=true to return only the live arbitrages. Built for trading agents that poll for tradeable spreads: informational only, verify each market's exact resolution rules, fees, and withdrawal terms before trading. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

arbs_only.description: When true, return only events with a live arbitrage right now (combined cost under $1). Default false returns the full matched-events board.

tools.name: create_market_map
tools.description: Build a startup market map from a plain-language request, e.g. 'fintech startups in London' or 'AI coding assistants split by use case'. The map splits the market into segments and fills each with real companies from StartupHub.ai's database of startup profiles, with their logos. Returns image_url (a PNG of the finished map: show it to the user), editor_url (open the map in Market Map Maker to edit it by hand or by chat), the segments with every company and its profile link, and the full map spec as JSON. Set publish: true to also get a public link. Uses one market map credit from the account's monthly allowance. Answers within about 15 seconds: when status is 'building' the map is saved and still filling, section by section, so follow it with get_market_map (map_id) every few seconds until status is 'done', not with another create_market_map (the interactive map view in Claude does this itself and shows each section as it fills). Same result as POST /api/v1/market-maps. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

tools.name: generate_startup_list
tools.description: Prompt → curated startup list. Caller can then hand those IDs to a separate /lists/submit call to publish the list as a public, indexed page. Useful workflows: (1) build a portfolio-style page from a prompt without manual curation, (2) extract a list of companies from raw text (paste a YC batch page, a16z portfolio, CSV: set 'pasted_list' instead of 'prompt'), (3) regularly refresh a 'who's new in X sector' list via cron. Each call costs 5 credits (Startup=15/day, Pro=50/day). Returns the matched startups (id/name/slug/logo) plus a 'created' count showing how many were brand new in our DB. tools.title: Search suggestions

tools.name: find_matches
tools.description: Find Matches. Given a startup slug or id, return investors that fit, each with a reason. Given an investor slug or id, return startups that fit. Requires an API key. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

slug.description: Profile slug of the startup or investor to match from. Pass slug or id.

id.description: Profile UUID of the startup or investor to match from. Pass slug or id.

tools.title: Find matches

tools.name: list_monitor_watches
tools.description: List company watches on this API key. Each watch covers pricing, jobs, news, and the other signals that plan allows. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).
tools.title: List monitor watches

tools.name: create_monitor_watch
tools.description: Monitor. Watch a company site and get alerts when public signals change. Pass a domain. Optional frequency: weekly, daily, 12h, or 4h, clamped to the plan. Optional signals. Optional webhook_url (https). Requires an API key. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).

signals.description: Subset of: news, funding, jobs, tech_stack, pricing, status, leadership, customers, product_launches.

webhook_url.description: https URL that receives an alert when something changes.

tools.title: Create monitor watch

tools.name: cancel_monitor_watch
tools.description: Stop a company watch. Pass id from list_monitor_watches. Needs a StartupHub.ai API key with credit (pay as you go).
tools.title: Cancel monitor watch

resources.name: Market map view
resources.description: Interactive StartupHub.ai market map: the map as Market Map Maker draws it, with style, export, publish and a box to ask for changes.
